fieldMarks: Larger than a cottontail: about 18-20 in long, 1.2-1.8 kg.
Very large, heavily furred hind feet with widely spreading toes.
Grey-brown to yellowish-brown in summer with white underparts; almost pure white in winter (hairs dusky at the base); hind feet often stay white into summer.
Ear tips dark; ears smaller than most hares'.
In humid coastal southwestern B.C., Washington and Oregon they stay brown all year.
behavior: Most active from sundown to dawn and active all winter; rests by day in sheltered 'forms' under bushes, stumps or logs.
Keeps a network of well-maintained runways that follow the same routes summer and winter and become conspicuous after snowfall.
Eats herbaceous plants and shrub leaves in summer; twigs, buds and bark of conifers, aspen and willow in winter.
Populations cycle between high abundance and scarcity; generally silent but snorts, and clicks during breeding season.
habitat: Boreal forest and its southern mountain extensions; prefers dense understory of young trees or tall shrubs, including mixed spruce forest, wooded swamps and brushy areas.
range: Found in every Canadian province and territory and in Alaska, south along the Appalachians and the Rocky and Cascade mountains to North Carolina, New Mexico and California.
